title: 199 to 999 users and Redis stampede
hook: The attempt-submit path that was fine at 199 concurrent users fails at 999 in a specific way: every request misses the cache together, stampedes Redis or the origin, and if you ‘fixed’ it with a lock around I/O, you serialized the entire fleet.

sections.heading: What breaks at 999
sections.prose: At 199 concurrent submits, a 5 ms Redis GET and a rare miss to the origin hide a lot of sins: a static Dictionary, a lock around the miss, a sync-over-async client. At 999, misses cluster after TTL expiry (especially a deploy that flushes keys). Thread-pool injection lags. Server GC sees a gen-0 spike from per-request buffers. A lock(_gate) around StringGetAsync either deadlocks on await or, if you block, makes 999 users share one round-trip at a time. The fix is single-flight per cache key: the first miss creates a Task that fills Redis; everyone else awaits that Task. Mutation of the in-flight map uses ConcurrentDictionary or a tiny lock that does not include the I/O. TTL jitter (expiry plus random 0–30s) stops lockstep expiry. SemaphoreSlim(8) can cap origin load if the fill is a database, still without holding a Monitor during the query.

snippets.label: Single-flight Redis fill without locking I/O
snippets.explanation: GetOrAdd still can start two fills in a tight race; for interviews mention CompareExchange of a Task or a keyed SemaphoreSlim(1) if the origin must run exactly once. Never lock around the awaits.

sections.heading: How this sits next to async and GC
sections.prose: Module 13 already told you to await Redis and pass CancellationToken so a shutdown at 999 in-flight submits cancels cleanly. Module 14 told you not to allocate a 200 KB payload per miss on the LOH. This module adds: do not serialize those awaits with a lock, do not Task.Run the GET, and do not use a process-wide Mutex. If SkiaSharp preview generation is on the same path, push it through a bounded Channel so CPU work cannot take all pool threads from I/O completions. The senior sentence: scale from 199 to 999 is cache coherency plus pool health plus GC, not ‘add more locks.’

interviewTakeaways: Stampede: thundering herd on TTL or cold cache. Single-flight a shared Task per key.
Never lock across Redis. Lock or ConcurrentDictionary only for the in-flight map.
Jitter TTLs, bound CPU offload, watch thread-pool starvation and LOH together.
commonPitfalls: lock around the entire GetOrCreate including HTTP.
MemoryCache without stampede protection (GetOrCreate is not single-flight across all versions/patterns).
Flushing all Redis keys on deploy, guaranteeing a herd.

jsTsCorrelations.note: A Map<string, Promise<T>> in Node is the same single-flight idea. The JS version cannot data-race the Map on one thread, but it can still stampede if you forget to store the Promise before awaiting.
